reason: The question “Has the company implemented multi-factor authentication systems?” was answered “MFA implemented only on some systems.” This is consistent with, rather than contradicted by, the documented situation: MFA is active for ordinary operations-management application accounts, the jump-host path, VPN and email, but is absent from the legacy RDP maintenance account and two active cloud-console administrative accounts (AR-07, AR-04). The approved risk assessment defines the relevant scope as the operations management system and administrative cloud environment and requires MFA for every enabled account on both (AR-01); the authentication-method assessment likewise requires MFA for all accounts on those systems, with no documented derogations for the uncovered accounts (AR-07, AR-04). PR.AA-03_P2 requires MFA for at least the relevant systems in accordance with the risk assessment. ENISA particularly identifies remote and system-administration access as appropriate MFA use cases (V5-ENISA-0051-02). Thus, implemented MFA covers part of the applicable scope, but the specifically identified remote-maintenance and administrative-account gaps violate the risk-based coverage required by PR.AA-03_P2; partial satisfaction is appropriate because MFA is demonstrably implemented elsewhere within that scope (AR-07).
